claims: Automated bid submission worked across several online portals
Burned through all tokens in about 1-2 hours because bidding is document-intensive
Giving the agent its own computer means handing over the keys to all your access -- do at your own risk
Next plan: Hermes harness + open-weight models on a 4090, escalate to Claude/Codex/Groq only for heavy lifts
how_to_steps: Install grokbot (Hermes-style agent with no configuration)
Log in to each bid portal inside the agent's own computer
Let the agent read solicitation documents, check qualification, and submit bids
Monitor token usage; move document-heavy reading to a local open-weight model
on_screen_only: Overlay text: 'Automating the bid process' / 'Government contracting' (talking-head only, no screens shown)

relevance.why: As a veteran-owned founder, government contracting is a plausible channel; this is a candid field report on cost (token burn) and security trade-offs of agentic bid automation rather than a tutorial.

implement_score.why: Lesson is reusable: route document-heavy reading to cheap/local models and keep Claude for judgment; but the specific 'grokbot' tool and handing portal credentials to an autonomous agent are not advisable without vetting.

verify: What 'grokbot' is (xAI product? third-party?) and its pricing/security model
Legality of automated submissions on SAM.gov and agency portals (ToS, bot rules)
Which open-weight models fit a 24 GB 4090 for long-document reading
